makurakotoba.conventional_meaning: conventional epithet for sky, heaven, moon, light — evokes the vast celestial realm

jokotoba.text: わたの原こぎ出でて見れば
jokotoba.function: Sets up the scene of rowing out onto the vast sea and looking around, establishing the visual perspective from which the shimo-no-ku's image of distant clouds and whitecaps is perceived; not a fixed epithet but a freely composed scene-setting preface leading into the perception of the horizon.

kigo.note: Whitecaps on the open sea (沖つ白波) are conventional waka imagery of the vast ocean rather than a seasonally marked image; the poem as a whole lacks a specific seasonal marker — it is a poem of grand natural scenery (sea and sky) composed for a screen painting, without blossoms, autumn leaves, snow, or other seasonal cues. Listed here as the dominant image though it does not carry seasonal weight.

bipartite.kami_theme: The speaker rows out onto the vast open sea and looks around at the surrounding scene.
bipartite.shimo_theme: The white waves on the open sea appear to merge with and wander among the distant clouds on the horizon.
bipartite.pivot_note: The kami-no-ku's act of rowing out and looking (見れば) is the perceptual trigger; the shimo-no-ku reveals what is seen — the startling visual confusion of sea and sky, where the whitecaps seem to blend into the clouds at the horizon line, collapsing the boundary between sea and heaven.
